comment: The decisive miss was late-budget test-CE risk: D’s aggressive, nearly unregularized AdamW recipe finished last, even behind slow B and C; conservative Adagrad A also beat regularized Adam E. Excess confidence or distractor fitting could explain this, but ordinal results cannot establish either mechanism. I overextended K1002/K1003’s undertraining preferences and underweighted K1001/K1073’s saturation warnings. Backtesting found conservative recipes winning only 2/9 same-model long-budget history comparisons across seven questions. In long-budget smooth-additive lab comparisons, lower-rate AdamW won 12/17 pairs across three sets; five reversed. No exact long-budget zero-LN ReLU lab controls matched this question. These results support conditional caution, not a tested rule predicting the complete gold order.

  else:

   win=order.index(b[0])<order.index(a[0])
  rule=re.search(r'Rule family: `([^`]+)',q)
  records.append((r['question_id'],rule[1] if rule else '?',T,a[2],a[3],b[2],b[3],win))
print('records',len(records)); print('long', [x for x in records if x[2]>=1024]); print('short', [x for x in records if x[2]<1024]);"}
